description: The validate_script function calls fancy_regex::Regex::new to check syntax of :regex patterns at compile time, but fancy_regex does not detect exponential backtracking (ReDoS). A crafted pattern like '(a+)+b' or '(x*)*y' will compile successfully but execute in exponential time on adversarial input. The lib.rs ReDoS note documents this and delegates mitigation to a sieve_eval_timeout_ms config option -- but that config option is described as future work and is not enforced in evaluate(). If operators accept Sieve scripts from untrusted sources (e.g. user-uploaded scripts via JMAP), there is no runtime CPU bound. The fix is to either: (a) implement the eval timeout before accepting untrusted scripts, or (b) document clearly that untrusted script upload must be disabled until the timeout is wired.
title: sieve: ReDoS via :regex patterns accepted at compile time; no backtracking budget enforced
